description: Export material keys (measurements.json `materials`, shared/README.md) -> hand-made Unreal materials (#2282). tools/unreal-engine/python/import_world.py replaces every imported material instance whose key matches a rule (first match wins, Python regex on the key; an optional `mesh` regex also has to match the StaticMesh asset name, which is the id of the first export node using that mesh). Keys that match no rule keep Interchange's glTF material instance, which carries the key's colour, roughness, metalness, opacity and emissive. tools/unreal-engine/python/build_materials.py builds every entry under `materials` (masters first, then instances). `scope` and `defaults` drive the key-coverage check in tools/unreal-engine/tests/test_materials.py: every key on a building or ground node of the export must match a rule or a default with a reason. `source` names where the web takes the look from; `assumption` carries plan-material's *guess* markers into the asset metadata (Lunden.Source / Lunden.Assumption).

scope.note: Building and ground surfaces: every export node that is not furniture, interactive, light, collision or fixture. The `structure` kind also holds fixed fittings (kitchen, bathroom, radiators, vents, curtains); their keys are covered by rules or explicit defaults too.

vertexColor.note: #2321: Interchange's glTF masters multiply COLOR_0 only in their base-colour-texture branch (static switch bHasBaseColorTexture), so an untextured vertex-coloured key (`_vc`: three.js vertexColors, the export keeps the colour attribute) with a white or light base colour came out white. After the rules, import_world.py re-parents every imported instance whose key matches `match` and that has no base colour texture from its Interchange master onto the listed project copy (the instance keeps its parameters and its parent chain's blend/two-sided overrides). An unlisted master fails the import; tests/test_materials.py fails when an export key with vertex colours would get a master without vertex colour, in any zone.

unlitLabel.note: #2435: the web draws its signs and labels unlit (MeshBasicMaterial with a colour map: the flats' number signs, name plates and door leaves in Hus A, B, C and L, the stairwells' floor numbers and exit pictograms, the garage's sign plates, floor markings and plans, the scoreboards, screens and printed labels), so a plate shows whiter than the wall beside it and reads as well in the dark. The export keeps each with its image (#2400) and KHR_materials_unlit, and marks it in measurements.json materials[] (`unlit`, `powerCut`: the share of its colour a power cut leaves on the web). After the rules and the vertex colours, import_world.py re-parents every such instance from Interchange's unlit master (`from`) onto `master` and sets its PowerCut parameter; --check and tests/test_materials.py fail when such a key would render lit.

instanceOverrides.note: #2440: changes to Interchange's own instance of a key that no rule replaces, so it keeps the export's colour, roughness, metalness and emissive. import_world.py applies each entry (first match on the key wins; `zones` limits it to those zones' instances) after the rules and vertex colours and before the Nanite step; --check verifies it. `blend: "opaque"` draws a translucent key opaque; `masters` re-parents the instance from its Interchange master onto a listed `gltf-surface-forward` copy (Surface ForwardShading translucency) and keeps the parent chain's blend and two-sided overrides. Interchange's masters light translucent instances from the translucency volume (TLM_SURFACE): in the patio view of 21 June at 14:00 it lit the beer at about 0.3 of the same colour drawn opaque and gave its glass a blue sky veil (docs/verification/2440/). tests/test_materials.py checks the entries against the export.

entries.reason: the patio beer (src/patio.js beerMat, 88 % opaque with a faint orange emissive): on Interchange's translucent instance it came out grey-brown (sRGB 108, 87, 73 against the web's 176, 131, 55). Drawn opaque it keeps the export's colour and emissive and is lit like any surface; the 12 % see-through to the glass bottom is dropped

the patio pint glasses (src/patio.js glassMat, 24 %): the translucency volume lights them with blue sky light, which laid a grey-blue veil over the beer (R/B 2.2 against the web's 3.2 with the beer opaque); Surface ForwardShading gives R/B 3.6. The same key on the Bestå's crystal glasses in l1007 (src/furniture.js crystal) keeps Interchange's master until the general translucent lighting is settled (#2459)
